title: Execution and Evaluation: Task Content, Labor Demand, and the Evaluator Pipeline
abstract: arXiv:2607.20807v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Measures of occupational AI exposure ask whether machines can perform a task, not which function the human supplies. I distinguish execution, producing a first-pass output, from evaluation, judging whether it is correct, and make the distinction measurable by scoring all 19,265 O*NET task statements under fixed rubrics. The execution score is reproducible across model coders and O*NET vintages. In a 200-task random audit it correlates 0.81 with the mean of four blinded human coders. It predicts each held-out coder's peers better than that coder does, though the coders disagree substantially among themselves. It adds only modest power beyond O*NET's evaluation activities. Employment growth is lower in execution-heavy white-collar occupations in every window since 2012; the gradient shows no post-2022 break and lies largely between occupational families. translated_title: 执行与评估：任务内容、劳动力需求与评估者流水线
translated_abstract: 职业AI暴露度的测量方法关注的是机器能否执行某项任务，而非人类在其中提供的是哪种功能。本文区分了执行（产出初版输出）与评估（判断输出是否正确）两种功能，并通过对全部19,265条O*NET任务描述在固定评分标准下进行打分，使这一区分变得可测量。执行评分在不同模型编码员和不同O*NET版本之间具有可复现性。在一项包含200个任务的随机审计中，该评分与四名盲评人类编码员的均值相关系数达到0.81；它对每位留出编码员的同行预测得比该编码员本人更好，尽管编码员彼此之间存在显著分歧。相比O*NET原有的评估类活动，该评分仅增加了有限的解释力。研究还发现，自2012年以来的每个时间段内，以执行为主的白领职业就业增长都更低；这一梯度在2022年后并未出现断点，且主要体现在职业大类之间。此外，Eloundou暴露度梯度在2022—2025年间比疫情期间更为陡峭。
tldr: 该论文首次将职业任务区分为“执行”与“评估”两类功能并构建可复现的量化评分体系，发现自2012年以来执行密集型白领职业的就业增长持续偏低，且AI暴露度与就业的负向梯度在2022年后并未出现断裂。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a reproducible scoring framework that separates occupational tasks into "execution" and "evaluation" functions, showing that execution-heavy white-collar occupations have experienced persistently lower employment growth since 2012 with no post-2022 break in the AI exposure gradient.
